questions.question: A point on the y-axis must have:
solutionSteps: The y-axis has no horizontal displacement from the origin.
Every point on it therefore has x-coordinate 0.

questions.question: The midpoint of (−5,−2) and (1,4) is:
solutionSteps: Average the respective coordinates, not cross-coordinates.

questions.question: Derive the distance formula for A(x₁,y₁) and B(x₂,y₂) using a right triangle. Apply it to A(−3,−2) and B(5,4).
questions.finalAnswer: AB = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²); the example distance is 10.
solutionSteps: Draw horizontal and vertical segments between the two points to form a right triangle.
Their lengths are |x₂ − x₁| and |y₂ − y₁|.
Pythagoras gives the squared distance as the sum of the two squared coordinate differences.
For the example, the differences are 8 and 6; √(64 + 36) = 10.

questions.question: M(3,−1) is the midpoint of A(−2,4) and B. Find B and state its quadrant.
solutionSteps: (−2 + xB)/2 = 3 gives xB = 8.
(4 + yB)/2 = −1 gives yB = −6.
A positive x and negative y place B in Quadrant IV.

questions.question: Describe a systematic algorithm to check if three distinct coordinate points form a triangle, and then whether that triangle is right-angled. Test A(1,1), B(4,1), C(4,5).
questions.finalAnswer: The points form a triangle right-angled at B.
solutionSteps: First test collinearity, for example whether (xB − xA)(yC − yA) = (yB − yA)(xC − xA). If equal, there is no non-degenerate triangle.
For the given points the products are 12 and 0, so they are not collinear.
Compute the three squared distances: AB² = 9, BC² = 16, AC² = 25.
Sort these values. The two smaller sum to the largest, so the angle at B is right.

questions.question: On a floor-plan grid, a straight corridor joins P(−1,2) to Q(7,8), with each unit representing 0.5 m. Find its actual length and the coordinates of a camera placed halfway along it.
solutionSteps: The grid displacement is (8,6), so the grid length is √100 = 10.
Multiply by the scale 0.5 m per unit to get 5 m.
The halfway coordinates are ((−1 + 7)/2, (2 + 8)/2) = (3,5).
Coordinates remain in grid units; do not multiply them by the physical length scale unless explicitly converting the coordinate system.

questions.question: Explain why an ordered pair must be ordered. Plot P(2,5) and Q(5,2) and explain how coordinate geometry lets us compare their positions without relying on an approximate picture.
questions.finalAnswer: The first coordinate is horizontal and the second vertical; P and Q are different points.
solutionSteps: An ordered pair assigns different roles to its first and second entries.
P is 2 units right and 5 up; Q is 5 right and 2 up.
Subtracting coordinates gives Q − P = (3,−3). Algebra makes this comparison exact and independent of drawing accuracy.
